preAssetEventsWindow.description:
The default target variable for supervised {@link MlModel} is some time window leading
up to {@link ReliabilityAssetEvent}s. Usually, leading up to a {@link ReliabilityAssetEvent},
there will be signs of degradation. Defining all timestamps leading up to downtime events
as label=1 and all other timestamps as label=0 is one way of training supervised
{@link MlModel}s. This is the default approach to training supervised {@link MlModel}s for
the `reliabilityRisk` {@link MlProject}. Define the number of time steps appropriately,
based on the {@link ReliabilityMlDatasetPreparationSpec#interval}.
For example, the default {@link Interval} is `QUARTER_HOUR`. So, the default number of time
steps here is 288, which translates to 3 days leading up to {@link ReliabilityAssetEvent}s.

targetOverride.description:
If the user wishes to train supervised {@link MlModel}s for the `reliabilityRisk` {@link MlProject}
but does not want to employ the usage of the default target variable, use this field to
provide a {@link Feature} that will result in a trained {@link MlModel} that produces risk scores.
Note that the {@link Feature} provided here MUST be upserted and MUST have the `name` field
populated.

title:
If training and deploying supervised {@link MlModel}s for any {@link MlProject}s,
then use this spec to define the target variable. There can only be one target variable for an
{@link MlModel}.
name: ReliabilityMlTargetPreparationSpec
